title: GLASS Flows: Efficient Inference for Reward Alignment of Flow and Diffusion Models
claim: A pretrained model can be transformed into an inner flow that samples stochastic transitions efficiently, improving output alignment with the prompt.
layout: 2 panels: left trajectory diagram with vertical transform chain, right 3x2 image grid
description: The figure has two parts. On the left is a hand-drawn-style diagram of curved maroon trajectories. A black point x_t sits in the center, with dashed gray arrows leading to several Gaussian-sampled start points. The labels read 'Sample N(γ̄x_t, I_d)' and 'Start x̄_{s=0}'. Each start point flows along an arc to an end point at s=1, and one path ends at x_t'. A blue arrow marks the velocity u_s(x̄_s|x_t,t), and green labels mark s=0 and s=1. A vertical chain of black arrows sits in the middle. It runs from sufficient statistic S(x_t, x̄_s) through denoiser D_t to the pretrained flow matching model u_t, and a left-pointing 'Transform' arrow connects that model to the velocity. On the right is a grid of three rows of photos. Each row shows a 'Flow' image, a 'GLASS (Ours)' image and the text prompt. The prompts are 'a photo of a backpack right of a sandwich', 'a photo of a black kite and a green bear', and 'a photo of a tennis racket and a bicycle'. The baseline images miss objects or get the layout wrong, while the GLASS images show all the objects correctly. The eye goes first to the colorful photos and the large handwritten math labels.
caption: GLASS Flows overview. Left: Sampling transition $p_{t'|t}(x_{t'}|x_t)$ with GLASS Flows. Initial Gaussian samples $\bar{x}_{s=0}$ are evolved from inner time $s=0$ to $s=1$ via the velocity field $u_s(\bar{x}_s|x_t,t)$ that is obtained by transforming a pre-trained flow matching model. Right: Reward alignment with GLASS Flows improves text-image alignment.
abstract: The performance of flow matching and diffusion models can be greatly improved at inference time using reward adaptation algorithms, yet efficiency remains a major limitation. While several algorithms were proposed, we demonstrate that a common bottleneck is the sampling method these algorithms rely on: many algorithms require to sample Markov transitions via SDE sampling, which is significantly less efficient and often less performant than ODE sampling. To remove this bottleneck, we introduce GLASS Flows, a new sampling paradigm that simulates a ''flow matching model within a flow matching model'' to sample Markov transitions. As we show in this work, this ''inner'' flow matching model can be retrieved from any pre-trained model without any re-training, effectively combining the efficiency of ODEs with the stochastic evolution of SDEs. On large-scale text-to-image models, we show that GLASS Flows eliminate the trade-off between stochastic evolution and efficiency. GLASS Flows improve state-of-the-art performance in text-to-image generation, making it a simple, drop-in solution for inference-time scaling of flow and diffusion models.
